name: session-scoped-wrap-up
why: The canonical phrasing and the one said most often. Competes with reflect, which also claims wrap-up language - if this fails, the two descriptions are not separable and one has to give.

name: end-the-session
why: Session scope with no git vocabulary and no use of the word wrap. Checks the trigger is not keyed on a single phrase.

name: close-it-out
why: Directly overlaps reflect's current description, which claims 'close out the session'. This is the head-to-head case.

name: bare-wrap-up
why: No object stated. Ambiguous in principle but in practice means the session, and /wrap-up covers a wrong guess.

name: three-verbs-reflect-notes-push
why: Three of the five chain verbs named together. The shorthand form, no session word present.

name: three-verbs-notes-commit-sync
query: notes, commit, then sync it up
why: A different three of the five, in a different order, phrased as a sentence rather than a list.

name: end-of-day
why: Session end implied rather than stated. The softest true case; a miss here is acceptable, a miss on the explicit ones is not.

name: task-scoped-wrap-up
query: let's wrap up this task and move on
why: The stated worry. Same verb, smaller object. Firing a three-gate session closeout on a task boundary is the main false-positive risk.

name: feature-scoped-closeout
query: close out this bug and we'll do the next one
why: Closeout language scoped to a unit of work, with an explicit signal that the session continues.

name: context-pressure
why: A warning, not an instruction. The right response is to report remaining room and offer the closeout, not to start it.

name: running-long
query: we're running long on this one
why: Same class as above, phrased about duration rather than context. Must not be read as a closeout request.

name: mid-session-commit
query: commit what we have so far so I don't lose it
why: A mid-session save is a plain commit. One verb, and the sentence says the session continues.

name: docs-only
query: update the docs with what we did
why: notes on its own. Should not escalate into memory writes and a push.

name: push-only
why: repo-device-sync owns a bare push intent. One verb is never the chain.
